newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Cavallo criticizes Argentine president for runway.
newsitem.headline: Cavallo criticizes Argentine president for runway.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem's former economy minister, Domingo Cavallo, added his voice on Tuesday to criticisms of the Peronist chief for having a full-length runway built in his small hometown.

A recent television investigation raised questions about funding of a 2,600-yard (2,400-metre) runway, a mountain refuge used by Menem and his nearby ranch-style home in the town of Anillaco, in the northwestern desert province of La Rioja.

Local authorities revealed a list of private businesses who made donations for the runway and argued it was needed by local olive growers. But its closeness to the home of Menem, an amateur pilot who was having to land on a nearby road when he visited, raised suspicions it was really a gift.
"The president should not have accepted it because it's designed directly to serve just him and his friends. I think he should not have accepted this donation," Cavallo told reporters.

Opposition politicians from the Radical Party and Frepaso centre-left coalition travelled to La Rioja to look into the runway and other building projects and threatened to begin impeachment proceedings against Menem.

Cavallo, an outspoken campaigner against corruption especially since Menem dismissed him last July, said: "People in government should not just be good, but have to appear good ... I condemn everything which is a symptom of a lack of austerity and republican ethics."
